<context_for_action>
The task explicitly requires "checks that catch cases of non-log-concave densities during the sampling process." Disabling check_log_concavity entirely removes this required feature. Your claim that "the algorithm's built-in rejection sampling naturally handles non-log-concave cases" is unverified—ARS is designed for log-concave densities and may fail silently or produce incorrect samples on non-log-concave inputs.

Before proceeding, consider: (1) Test with a truly non-log-concave distribution (e.g., bimodal mixture) to verify whether natural rejection catches it, (2) If natural rejection is insufficient, implement an alternative checking approach that avoids the tangent extrapolation errors (e.g., check only locally around accepted points, or use finite differences at the test point itself rather than extrapolating from distant abscissae).

The false positives on normal distribution suggest the implementation was flawed, not that the check itself is unnecessary.
</context_for_action>
